**Suspended NFL quarterback Michael Vick tested positive for marijuana while free on bond awaiting sentencing in his federal dogfighting case, according to court documents filed Wednesday.**

A federal judge responded to the failed drug test by imposing stricter conditions on Vick's pretrial release, including a curfew and electronic monitoring.

U.S. District Judge Henry E. Hudson ordered Vick to be confined to his home between the hours of 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. and to submit to electronic monitoring via an ankle bracelet. The former Atlanta Falcons star is also now restricted from consuming alcohol and must undergo random drug testing.

Vick submitted a urine sample on September 13 as part of the standard conditions of his release. The sample tested positive for marijuana, according to the court filing.

## Background on the Case

Vick pleaded guilty in August to a federal conspiracy charge related to his role in an interstate dogfighting operation known as "Bad Newz Kennels," which operated on his property in Surry County, Virginia.

The plea agreement detailed Vick's involvement in the financing of the dogfighting enterprise and his participation in the killing of dogs that underperformed. Prosecutors said dogs were executed by various methods, including hanging and drowning.

The case drew widespread condemnation from animal rights groups and sparked national outrage. The NFL suspended Vick indefinitely without pay following his guilty plea, and the Falcons sought to recover portions of his signing bonus.

## Looking Ahead to Sentencing

Vick faces sentencing on the federal conspiracy charge, with the possibility of prison time under federal guidelines. He also faces potential state charges in Virginia related to the dogfighting operation.

Three of Vick's co-defendants had previously pleaded guilty and cooperated with prosecutors in the case.

The positive drug test could complicate matters for Vick as he awaits sentencing, potentially influencing the judge's consideration of his conduct while on release.

Vick's attorneys did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

*This is a developing story.*

**SUSSEX, Virginia** — A suspended NFL quarterback was ordered to abide by tightened pretrial release conditions Thursday after a failed drug test, marking the latest setback in a legal saga that has kept the veteran signal-caller off the field for the entire season.

Appearing before a federal magistrate at the Sussex County courthouse, the quarterback stood quietly as the judge outlined new restrictions following the positive test result, which court documents indicated detected a controlled substance in violation of his bond terms.

Under the revised conditions, the athlete will be subject to electronic monitoring, a strict curfew, and expanded drug testing. He was also ordered to refrain from any travel outside the judicial district without prior court approval.

## Defense Responds

Speaking to reporters outside the courthouse, the quarterback's lead defense attorney sought to downplay the severity of the violation while acknowledging the seriousness of the court's response.

"My client takes full responsibility for this lapse and understands the gravity of the situation," the attorney said. "This was an isolated mistake during an extraordinarily stressful period in his life. We are committed to demonstrating to the court that he will fully comply with every condition moving forward."

The attorney emphasized that his client remains focused on resolving the underlying case and eventually returning to professional football.

"He is a competitor, and he wants nothing more than to put this chapter behind him," the attorney added. "We respect the court's decision today and we intend to move forward in good faith. My client is receiving the support he needs, and we are confident that when all the facts are presented, people will see the full picture."

## A Season Sidelined

The quarterback has not played since being suspended by the league following his indictment earlier this year. The NFL placed him on the Commissioner's Exempt List, barring him from team activities while the case proceeds.

His absence has forced his club to shuffle its depth chart, thrusting a backup into the starting role and leaving the franchise's postseason hopes in question. Team officials have declined to comment on the ongoing legal proceedings, issuing only a brief statement noting they are "monitoring the situation closely."

## What Comes Next

Prosecutors argued that the failed drug test demonstrated a disregard for the conditions previously set, while the defense countered that no further liberty restrictions beyond the enhanced monitoring were warranted.

The magistrate ultimately stopped short of revoking bond entirely, allowing the quarterback to remain free ahead of trial provided he adheres to the new terms. A subsequent violation, the judge warned, could result in detention.

A trial date has not yet been finalized, though attorneys on both sides indicated proceedings could begin early next year.

For now, the quarterback's football future — and his freedom before trial — hinge on his ability to stay in compliance.

"We're taking this one day at a time," his attorney said. "Today was about accountability. Tomorrow is about proving he can meet the standard the court has set."
